newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Newcrest sells Normandy stake to ANZ.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Newcrest sells Normandy stake to ANZ.

text.p: Newcrest Mining Ltd said on Thursday that it had sold its 11.9 percent stake in Normandy Mining Ltd to Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd for a gold equivalent of A$1.75 per share under a two year equity-gold swap arrangement.
The company also said it would make a provision of A$134.7 million against its Normandy investment.
Newcrest said its stake in Normandy amounted to 192.7 million shares. At A$1.75 per Normandy share, this stake has a value of A$337.225 million.

Under the gold swap deal completed in late February, Newcrest said it would immediately receive the equivalent per-share value in gold, minus A$33 million which it would receive with interest in November this year.
"As part of the swap arrangement Newcrest will receive net cashflows which replicate an economic exposure to the Normandy shares in exchange for paying a lease rate on the gold," it said.
Newcrest said it had the option but not an obligation to repurchase the shares from ANZ during the two-year period.

At the end of the period, or perhaps earlier in certain circumstances, Newcrest said it would either receive or pay an amount which consisted of the net change in the market price of Normandy shares and the value of the gold in the swap transaction. It said it had purchased gold call options to manage its exposure.
"Newcrest believes the intrinsic value of Normandy is substantially higher than its current market value," the company said.
"Newcrest does not believe that it is appropriate to quit absolutely the investment at this time," the company said.
It said the swap deal had released funds tied up in the rival gold miner and allowed Newcrest to repay A$200 million of borrowings incurred when it first bought Normandy shares.
"The balance of these funds amounting to A$128.6 million will be used to progress Newcrest's development projects."
Normandy shares were steady at A$1.76 on Thursday, well below their 12-month high of A$2.70 and 22 cents above their low for the period.

Newcrest bought its Normandy stake in February 1996 in a futile attempt to both merge with its rival and to prevent Normandy from merging with its listed associates to form Australia's largest gold mining house.
Newcrest paid more than A$2.60 per share for its holding in Normandy.
